name: Response
summary: Standard smoothing for fast aim. Higher makes the reticle feel lighter at speed.

where.text: Edit your Config (pencil icon). In Mouse Aim or Motion Aim, set Smoothing to Custom instead of a preset, and make sure the smoothing button reads STANDARD (press it to change modes). Response is one of the Standard settings.

citations.quote: To edit the current Config, press the pencil icon.
Here you can set Sensitivity (remember that lower values are faster) and Smoothing.
Motion aim settings consists of Sensitivity and Smoothing.
You can also customize the smoothing system and choose between two smoothing modes: Standard and Classic.
It's recommended you use one of the smoothing presets. If you are using "custom", ensure you do not reduce smoothing intensity below that of the presets.
Press the the smoothing button (i.e. "STANDARD" or "CLASSIC") to change modes.

definition.text: Controls fast aim behavior. Higher values produces a lighter feeling reticle at faster aim speeds.

citations.quote: Higher values produces a lighter feeling reticle at faster aim speeds.

plainWords.text: It acts on fast movements: big turns and quick moves onto a target. Raising it makes the reticle feel lighter during those movements.

citations.quote: Higher values produces a lighter feeling reticle at faster aim speeds.

plainWords.text: Lowering it should make fast movements feel heavier.

citations.quote: Higher values produces a lighter feeling reticle at faster aim speeds.

plainWords.reasoning: The guide only describes raising it ("a lighter feeling reticle at faster aim speeds"). Lowering it is the reverse.

plainWords.text: The guide doesn't give this setting's range or default. Check what Manager shows before you change it.

feel.text: Higher Response gives a lighter-feeling reticle at faster aim speeds.

citations.quote: Higher values produces a lighter feeling reticle at faster aim speeds.

guidance.text: The guide gives no recommended value for this setting. It says smoothing is "strictly based on preference" and suggests trying the presets first.

citations.quote: Both mouse and motion have different presets designed for those aiming methods. Start by trying each out to see what feels most natural to you. It's strictly based on preference.

aimStyles.text: Snap: a secondary lever, for the fast part of a snap or flick. The main snap lever is Easing, which shapes the start from rest. If fast moves feel too heavy, raise Response; if they feel too light, lower it.

citations.quote: Higher values produces a lighter feeling reticle at faster aim speeds.

aimStyles.reasoning: Snaps are fast movements, and Response "Controls fast aim behavior", with higher values giving "a lighter feeling reticle at faster aim speeds". A snap starts from rest, and Easing "Specifies aim behavior from rest", so Primer treats Easing as the main snap lever and Response as the second.

aimStyles.text: Tracking: matters when the target moves fast or you turn quickly while firing. Slow holds depend more on Precision.
aimStyles.reasoning: Response acts at fast aim speeds; Precision acts at low aim speeds.

confusions.name: Response rate (Check Rate)
confusions.note: A Manager tool that counts how often your mouse actually reports movement, to check its polling rate. It is not a smoothing setting.

confusions.name: Aim response curve
confusions.note: The guide calls an aiming curve your "aim response". That is the Aiming Curve, not this setting.

confusions.name: "Response time" in Easing
confusions.note: Easing's definition mentions "response time" for the start from rest. That describes Easing, not the Response setting.
